fact_check_verdict: Core survives with hedges. Forum claims are News-Miner single-source (attribute). Governor positions are Sept (Beacon). Senate bill is Beacon. CUT: forum date as 'a week out', Sullivan/RPM, $500M figure, ADN op-ed platform items (opinion), donor story, SB 250 number, Taylor 'bring their own energy', any claim of every race or AI-specific bill.

claims.spoken: Early voting began October nineteenth, and Election Day is November third.
requires: Alaska Beacon Oct 24th, corroborated by Alaska Public Media voter guide. Oct 19th, not 20th.
claims.verbatim_source: Election Day is Nov. 3 and early voting in Alaska began on Oct. 19.

claims.spoken: This fall, Alaska's candidates are being asked about data centers.
requires: Framing line, supported by c3, c8 to c13. Not a claim about every race.
claims.verbatim_source: Where do Alaska's four governor candidates stand on data centers? (headline); candidates ... generally agreed ... during a Tanana Valley League of Women Voters forum

claims.spoken: At a Fairbanks area forum, twelve statehouse candidates generally agreed that big data centers need rules and local input, per the Fairbanks Daily News-Miner.
requires: Attribute to the Fairbanks Daily News-Miner, Jack Barnwell, Oct 18th. Say Interior or Fairbanks area, never statewide. Hedge: generally agreed, some regulatory framework.
claims.verbatim_source: Decisions regarding large-scale data centers should have some regulatory framework and include local input.

claims.spoken: Then they split on how.
requires: Transition from c3 to c5 to c7. Source is the News-Miner.
claims.verbatim_source: The split was in how favorable they were

claims.spoken: Three of them, Carrick, McFarland and Dibert, backed a state moratorium until Alaska can study the issue.
requires: Democratic incumbent Ashley Carrick House 35, independent Pepper McFarland House 33, Democratic incumbent Maxine Dibert House 31. A state moratorium with an until condition, never a ban.
claims.verbatim_source: Carrick, McFarland and Dibert favored placing a state moratorium on any data center development until Alaska can thoroughly study...

claims.spoken: Republican Jeff Rentzel favored some sort of tax on data centers and on automation.
claims.on_screen: RENTZEL · A TAX ON DATA CENTERS
requires: Republican Jeff Rentzel, House 35. Keep the hedge some sort of. No rate given.
claims.verbatim_source: He also favored some sort of tax on AI data centers and automation (robotic or self-checkouts) in general.

claims.spoken: Republican Aimee Moore said they could pay every Alaskan a digital dividend.
requires: Republican Aimee Moore House 31. Digital dividend is her quote, attribute to her.
claims.verbatim_source: "They could also pay us a digital dividend to each Alaskan," she said.

claims.spoken: Republican Harmony Tomaszewski said the grid isn't ready, and cited Golden Valley Electric's recent energy alert.
requires: Harmony Tomaszewski, Republican House 34 (article misspells Tomazewski). Say Golden Valley Electric. No alert details.
claims.verbatim_source: She cited Golden Valley Electric Association's recent energy alert. / doesn't have the electrical power infrastructure to accommodate large-scale AI data centers

claims.spoken: Others, like Republicans Mike Prax and Barbara Haney, said zoning is a job for local government.
requires: Republicans Mike Prax incumbent and Barbara Haney, House 33.
claims.verbatim_source: it's more appropriate for local government to be involved than state government.

claims.spoken: In one South Anchorage House race, independent Representative Ky Holland wants purpose built, modest sized data centers.
requires: ADN, Mari Kanagy, dated Oct 22nd. District 9. Holland a one-term independent. Do not call the race AI.
claims.verbatim_source: I'm excited about what we can be doing with purpose-built, strategic, modest-sized, more traditional data centers.

claims.spoken: His Republican opponent, John Boyle, is more open to large ones, especially on the North Slope.
claims.on_screen: BOYLE · OPEN TO LARGE, NORTH SLOPE
requires: Boyle works for STAK Energy, which proposes a North Slope data center. Drop the $500 million figure.
claims.verbatim_source: Boyle is more open to the possibility of large-scale data centers, especially on the North Slope,

claims.spoken: Both see data centers as a way to attract energy investment.
requires: Counterweight to the split framing.
claims.verbatim_source: Both candidates see the potential for data centers to attract investment in energy infrastructure.

claims.spoken: For governor, Republican Dave Bronson said in September, I'm a big believer in data centers.
requires: Said at a Commonwealth North forum in September. Say said in September.
Plate carries SAID IN SEPTEMBER.
Party label Republican per the Alaska Beacon Oct 24th AFN report, which names Bronson and Taylor as Republicans and Wilson as the Republican.
claims.verbatim_source: I'm a big believer in data centers. I know that might be unpopular with some folks here,

claims.spoken: Republican Treg Taylor said, we need to embrace it.
requires: September 8th forum. Say said in September.
Party label Republican per the Alaska Beacon Oct 24th AFN report, which names Bronson and Taylor as Republicans and Wilson as the Republican.
claims.verbatim_source: "I think we need to embrace it," he said of data centers.

claims.spoken: Republican governor candidate Bernadette Wilson wrote in September that she will never allow Alaska to be littered with hyperscale data centers.
requires: Written answer in September. Quote only the hyperscale line.
Party label Republican per the Alaska Beacon Oct 24th AFN report, which names Bronson and Taylor as Republicans and Wilson as the Republican.
claims.verbatim_source: I will never allow Alaska to be littered with hyperscale data centers that take our resources and spoil our lands.

claims.spoken: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins said he supports a moratorium until the Legislature passes a regulatory framework.
requires: Alaska Beacon Sep 18th, forum Sep 8th. Say said in September. Platform items from the ADN opinion column are cut.
claims.verbatim_source: I support a moratorium on data center development in Alaska until the Legislature can pass a comprehensive regulatory framework for that development in Alaska,

claims.spoken: This year, the Alaska Senate voted fourteen to five to pass a data center bill.
requires: Alaska Beacon Sep 18th. A data center bill, not an AI bill. Do not name SB 250 aloud.
claims.verbatim_source: This year, the Alaska Senate voted 14-5 to pass a data center bill,

claims.spoken: The House never took it up before the session ended.
requires: Never say voted down or killed. No House vote happened.
claims.verbatim_source: but the House failed to take it up before the end of the legislative session.

claims.spoken: It would have regulated how data centers use electricity from public utilities, and required decommissioning plans.
requires: Not an AI bill.
claims.verbatim_source: That bill would have regulated how data centers can use electricity from public utilities | and would have required them to create decommissioning plans.

claims.spoken: Its sponsor, Senator Loki Tobin, returns next year, and the Beacon expects the next governor to face similar legislation.
requires: Löki with umlaut on screen. The forecast is the Beacon's, attribute it.
claims.verbatim_source: The sponsor of the bill, Sen. Löki Tobin, D-Anchorage, will return to the Legislature next year,

claims.spoken: The governor candidates' positions are from September, and the forum is from mid October.
requires: Dating honesty line.
claims.verbatim_source: Beacon Sep 18th; News-Miner Oct 18th
